This section gathers the AffineDrift material on tangent-space formulations for nonlinear dynamics, contraction-style reasoning, and related control questions. It is exploratory work. The central local claim is that, at a fixed state and contact mode, the mapping from applied generalized forces to instantaneous generalized acceleration is linear within the tangent description being used. Finite-time conclusions require additional assumptions and error analysis; they do not follow automatically from the local statement alone.

::: {.callout-warning}
## Provenance and status

This series is original AffineDrift synthesis and has not been peer reviewed. The linearity of the tangent map and the use of local linear approximations are standard ingredients in differential geometry and mechanics. The site's additional interpretive claims about force attribution, accumulation over time, and control design should be read as in-development arguments, not settled results.
:::

## How to Read This Material

- Start with the [series landing and table of contents](../articles/Tangent%20Hyperplane%20Articles/TABLE_OF_CONTENTS.html) if you want the full exploratory package.
- Use the [Critiques and Responses](../critiques/index.html) section alongside these pages; it contains the main limitations and objections that currently matter most.
- If you want the textbook-style continuation of this line of work, use the [Tangent Hyperplane Contraction](../articles/tangent-hyperplane-contraction/index.html) workspace.

## Main Entries

- [Part I: Tangent Hyperplanes Unified Thesis](../articles/Tangent%20Hyperplane%20Articles/Tangent_Hyperplanes_Unified_Thesis.html): main statement of the framework and its intended implications.
- [Part II: Contraction Theory Meets Tangent Spaces](../articles/Tangent%20Hyperplane%20Articles/Advanced/Contraction_Tangent_Unification.html): explores links between differential stability arguments and local optimal-control structure.
- [Part III: Hybrid Tangent Spaces](../articles/Tangent%20Hyperplane%20Articles/Advanced/Hybrid_Tangent_Spaces.html): extends the discussion to systems with discrete mode changes.
- [Part IV: Residual-Aware Control](../articles/Tangent%20Hyperplane%20Articles/Advanced/Residual-Aware_Control.html): examines controller-design ideas that keep curvature and residual terms explicit.
- [Tangent Hyperplane Contraction](../articles/tangent-hyperplane-contraction/index.html): web-first chapter workspace that develops related material in a textbook format.

## Scope Limits

- The strongest statements here are local statements about instantaneous mappings and linearized objects.
- Claims about finite-time superposition, accumulated error, or controller performance depend on how residual terms are bounded and how mode changes are handled.
- The hybrid and contraction-oriented extensions remain under active development.
